dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the order-sensitive `tuple(payload) == _PAUSE_KEYS` pause check with an order-independent key-set comparison (or add a reordered-key regression test) so a future emit-site key reorder cannot silently disable pause recognition and cause delivery during a pause.
evidence: src/rebar/_bridge_runner.py:141: `and tuple(payload) == _PAUSE_KEYS`
Emit site is a separate module/dict literal: src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/__main__.py:176-181 builds `status = {"paused": True, "reason": ..., "who": ..., "paused_at": ...}`
Tests in tests/scripts/test_run_reconcile_bridge_heldout.py:69-88 cover non-JSON, missing keys, and paused:false, but no case exercises reordered keys, so the order-coupling is unguarded
dropped.finding: `_is_valid_pause_marker` recognizes a pause only when the parsed JSON keys appear in exactly the order `("paused","reason","who","paused_at")` (`tuple(payload) == _PAUSE_KEYS`). This silently couples to the dict-literal key order at the emit site in `rebar_reconciler.__main__` (lines 176-181). If that emit order is ever changed, pauses stop being recognized and the runner proceeds to strict delivery during an operator pause, with no error. A set/subset comparison would be equally strict on key presence without the ordering fragility.
dropped.suggested_fix: Compare key sets instead of the ordered tuple: `set(payload) == set(_PAUSE_KEYS)` (keep the existing per-value type/truthiness checks).

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm whether `REBAR_RECONCILER_FAIL_SILENT_NOOP: "1"` on the GitHub Run reconciler step is new drift (owned by ticket 48c8) vs pre-existing content preserved through the wrapper rewrite; if newly introduced, split it into its own ticket.
evidence: .github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml:261: `REBAR_RECONCILER_FAIL_SILENT_NOOP: "1"`
Inline comment (lines 255-261): 'The machinery landed default-off in df0ac80be (change 785); this flip turns it on for the live reconciler.'
tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_live_mode_failure_tally.py:21: '48c8-5375-f883-462d — REBAR_RECONCILER_FAIL_SILENT_NOOP=1 (ON in the live workflow)' — the flag belongs to a separate ticket

Ticket scope: 'This is an additive migration. Existing checked-out workflows ... keep their defaults, messages, mutation boundaries'; the held-out oracle test_bridge_primary_workflow_heldout.py only asserts the Run reconciler step equals 'rebar bridge run' and never requires this env
dropped.finding: The GitHub 'Run reconciler' step adds `REBAR_RECONCILER_FAIL_SILENT_NOOP: "1"`, flipping the live reconciler's silent-no-op/comment-error handling from advisory to hard failure. This is a live-behavior change owned by a different ticket (48c8-5375-f883-462d) and is not authorized by any AC of the referenced ticket, which promises only to extract a runner-neutral bridge entrypoint and thin the CI wrappers as an additive migration preserving defaults/messages/mutation boundaries.
dropped.suggested_fix: If this flag flip is introduced by this diff, move it into ticket 48c8-5375-f883-462d (its documented owner) rather than folding it into the bridge-entrypoint extraction; the wrapper-thinning change should preserve the reconciler's existing failure semantics.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Scope `actions: write` to only the continuous-loop path (e.g. move re-dispatch to a separate job with its own `permissions`, or document that clients should omit `actions: write` when RECONCILE_CONTINUOUS is unset).
evidence: `permissions:` block: `contents: write` and `actions: write    # re-dispatch this workflow to sustain the continuous loop (opt-in; see RECONCILE_CONTINUOUS)` at .github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml:58-60

The only consumer is the step at line 281-301 gated `if: ${{ !cancelled() && vars.RECONCILE_CONTINUOUS == 'true' }}` (line 295), which the docs describe as OFF by default ("Leave the Variable unset (the TEMPLATE default)", lines 22-23)
GitHub `permissions` cannot be scoped per-step, so an always-on `actions: write` is granted to the reconciler run (which pushes to the tickets branch) even in the default template configuration
dropped.finding: reconcile-bridge.yml grants workflow-level `actions: write` unconditionally, but that scope is only consumed by the opt-in re-dispatch step (gated on RECONCILE_CONTINUOUS == 'true', which the template default leaves off). The standing grant widens the token's blast radius for every scheduled/dispatch run even when the continuous loop is disabled.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider making ACLI_SHA256 mandatory (fail closed when unset) in the reconcile CI templates, matching the ACLI_VERSION pin already enforced.
evidence: .gitlab-ci.yml:33-37 — `if [ -n "${ACLI_SHA256:-}" ]; then ... sha256sum -c --strict; else echo "ACLI_SHA256 unset; downloaded acli was not checksum-verified" >&2; fi` (no exit on the else branch)
Jenkinsfile:60-64 mirrors the same warn-only-when-unset behavior
reconcile-bridge.yml:175-179 also only emits `::warning::ACLI_SHA256 unset` and continues
docs/jira-sync-setup.md:119 documents ACLI_SHA256 as "strongly recommended … warns if unset" — the warn-only posture is intentional and documented
dropped.finding: All three CI definitions download the acli tarball over the network and proceed WITHOUT verifying its integrity when ACLI_SHA256 is unset — the checksum step only warns and continues, so a compromised/tampered download would execute with Jira credentials.
